Matrix computation

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Estimate \AtlasInlineMath{\tau=\log\det(A)=\operatorname{tr}(\log A)}, with the matrix logarithm defined by spectral decomposition.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
Assume \AtlasInlineMath{A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0} and \AtlasInlineMath{A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}}, with \AtlasInlineMath{\mu I\preceq A\preceq\beta I}, \AtlasInlineMath{0<\mu\le\beta}, and \AtlasInlineMath{\beta/\mu\le\kappa}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
The information \AtlasInlineMath{d,\mu,\beta,\kappa,\eta,\delta} is public and \AtlasInlineMath{A} is hidden. Query \AtlasInlineMath{v\in\mathbb{R}^d} returns exact \AtlasInlineMath{Av}. Neither \AtlasInlineMath{\log(A)v} nor a shifted inverse action is available for free.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Return any real \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat\tau}. No explicit matrix logarithm, determinant, or verifiable certificate is required.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}
The base loss is \AtlasInlineMath{|\widehat\tau-\log\det(A)|}, with success threshold \AtlasInlineMath{\eta}. Positive eigenvalues ensure that the matrix logarithm and target are finite.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
Count right products with single vectors only: \AtlasInlineMath{N=N_{\mathrm r}}. A block of width \AtlasInlineMath{q} costs \AtlasInlineMath{q} calls.

The budget bounds calls for every fixed input and every private seed. Reading public inputs, exact real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are free. One call applies the interface to one vector.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
Algorithms may use private randomness and choose query vectors adaptively from the declared domain using all previous responses. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript; no Krylov or linear-span restriction applies. Exact internal arithmetic, storage, and communication are free in this oracle model. A block query is charged by its number of columns.

The algorithm is selected using public inputs only. For every admissible input fixed before generation of the private seed, success probability over private randomness is at least \AtlasInlineMath{1-\delta}.

\textbf{Budget convention.} A fixed worst-case budget respected for every input and private seed.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}
\AtlasInlineMath{d}: The order of the square input matrix and the dimension of each query vector. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1}.

\AtlasInlineMath{A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}}

\AtlasInlineMath{A\preceq\beta I_d}

\AtlasInlineMath{\beta/\mu\le\kappa}

\AtlasInlineMath{|\widehat\tau-\log\det A|\le\eta}

Success probability is at least \AtlasInlineMath{1-\delta}.

\AtlasInlineMath{A}: Hidden real symmetric positive definite matrix \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R^{d\times d}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log A}: Matrix logarithm defined by spectral decomposition \textbf{Domain:} Real symmetric matrix.

\AtlasInlineMath{A=U\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i)U^{\mathsf T}\ \Longrightarrow\ \log A=U\operatorname{diag}(\log\lambda_i)U^{\mathsf T}}

\AtlasInlineMath{\tau,\widehat\tau}: True log determinant and algorithmic estimate \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb R}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\tau=\log\det(A)=\sum_{i=1}^d\log\lambda_i(A)}

\AtlasInlineMath{s_\eta=\max\{1,\lceil8\eta^{-2}(d\log^2\kappa+2\eta\log\kappa)\log(2/\delta)\rceil\}}

\AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_i(A)}: Eigenvalues of a real symmetric or Hermitian matrix in nonincreasing order. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{1\le i\le d}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_1(A)\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_d(A)}

\AtlasInlineMath{\|z\|_2=(\sum_i|z_i|^2)^{1/2}}

\AtlasInlineMath{\|M\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\max_{\|z\|_2=1}\|Mz\|_2=\sigma_1(M)}

\AtlasInlineMath{\log}: Natural logarithm \textbf{Domain:} Positive real argument.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log x=\ln x}

\AtlasInlineMath{O,\Omega,\Theta}: Upper, lower, and two-sided bounds up to constants in the same applicable regime \textbf{Domain:} Hidden constants have only the parameter dependence explicitly permitted by the associated bound.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{4. Bounds and supporting evidence}
The following conditions apply to every bound in this profile, in addition to each bound's stated region and algorithm scope.

\textbf{Oracle mapping.} Only exact Av is available. Products log(A)v, linear solves, and preconditioners are not free interfaces. Each Lanczos iteration consumes one native right-product query.

\textbf{Guarantee mapping.} Success probability is at least 1 - $\delta$ for each fixed SPD input. Sampling and truncation parameters must use the same verified error allocation.

\textbf{Output mapping.} Return a real estimate of logdet(A) with absolute error at most $\eta$. Retain the public positive spectral interval $[\mu ,\beta ]$; relative log-determinant error is a different target.

\textbf{Resource mapping.} Count only right multiplication by a single vector, \AtlasInlineMath{N=N_{\mathrm r}}. A block product of width \AtlasInlineMath{q} costs \AtlasInlineMath{q} calls. The worst-case cap holds for every input and random seed; it is not an expected call count. Reading public inputs and exact internal arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged. This budget does not certify running time or bit complexity.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{B1 - Random Rademacher probes with stochastic Lanczos quadrature (SLQ)}
\textbf{Admission.} Included in the bracket

\textbf{Direction.} upper

\textbf{Witness or lower-bound scope.} Randomized witness

\AtlasMath{N\le s_\eta\min\{d,t_\eta\}}
\textbf{Sources.} \href{https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.10009v2}{[1]}

\textbf{Conditions.}

\AtlasMath{s_\eta=\max\{1,\lceil8\eta^{-2}(d\log^2\kappa+2\eta\log\kappa)\log(2/\delta)\rceil\}; t_\eta=\max\{1,\lceil\sqrt{\kappa+1}\log[4\eta^{-1}d(\sqrt{\kappa+1}+1)\log(2\kappa)]/4\rceil\}}
\textbf{Simultaneous resource costs.} All coordinates refer to this one witness or necessary constraint.

\textbf{N right.}

\AtlasMath{s_eta \min{d,t_eta}}
\textbf{probe count.}

\AtlasMath{s_eta}
\textbf{krylov steps per probe.}

\AtlasMath{\min{d,t_eta}}
\textbf{Constants.} Universal constants, with only the parameter dependence permitted by this bound’s region and expression.

\textbf{Derivation.} Each Lanczos step costs one Av product. If the Krylov subspace becomes invariant early, the quadratic form is computed exactly. Replacing the actual condition number kappa(A) by the public upper bound kappa only enlarges the two monotone sufficient budgets. Probe count and step count must arise from the same parameter choice.

\textbf{Source location.} \href{https://arxiv.org/pdf/2005.10009v2}{[1]} theorem: Theorem 20; Lemma 21; section: §4.2; pdf pages: 16; 17

The Rademacher construction avoids the additional Gaussian sample-count restriction in Theorem 19. The sampling bound in Lemma 21 does not depend on the sign of the log determinant.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{5. Local arguments}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{A1 - Deterministic reconstruction using the standard basis, followed by free exact solution of the target task}
\textbf{Scope.} All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

Recover the \AtlasInlineMath{d} columns of \AtlasInlineMath{A} by standard basis queries. Its positive spectrum permits exact internal evaluation of the sum of eigenvalue logarithms. The log-determinant error is zero, regardless of whether the log determinant itself is positive, zero, or negative.
